In 1997 a solid-fuel oxygen generator canister on Mir ignited, producing a three-foot flame, dense smoke, and blocking the route to a Soyuz escape vehicle. Investigators identified latex glove material introduced into the canister as the most likely cause of the Mir fire. The Mir crew donned oxygen masks and used foam fire extinguishers.

BASS-II crew-adapted flow variations, including blowoff extinctions, helped outline a U-shaped flammability boundary versus flow. BASS-II tested flows near the quenching limit, below those normally produced by ISS ventilation. For 0.1 mm PMMA, radiative quenching occurred below about 2 cm/s and blowoff extinction approached as flow crossed about 40 cm/s.

FLEX burned methanol and n-heptane droplets of 2 to 5 mm initial diameter at ambient temperature, 0.70 to 3.05 atm, with oxygen diluted by nitrogen, carbon dioxide or mixtures. Both radiative extinction (larger droplets, higher dilution) and diffusive extinction (smaller droplets) were observed in FLEX. Disruptive extinction of methanol droplets is probably caused by the contaminant, so disruption outcomes should be treated cautiously.

disclosure: HOLDOUT-2. Questions written on 2026-11-15 from passages of the original NASA publications in app/data/source_text (file and page given per question), before any run. Reference answers are taken from those passages. 'relevant' lists the curated library findings that state the reference fact; an empty list means the fact is in the publication but not in this library, so the correct system behaviour is to abstain. Written by the build assistant, who has seen the library: this is an internal holdout, not an independent one. Hash-locked in eval/HOLDOUT2.lock. Not used for tuning.
